messages.subject: Individual identification
parts:
Hi!

I was using the program but realized that I have a problem. I did the individual identification but when I get the summary of the data analyze, an individual is removed and not recognized. I checked the photos and noticed that there is a photo where  a female with her cub were identified. In the adult's individual directory, I put that photo (the one of the female and the cub) and in the cub's individual directory I put the same photo.

The problem is that when I run some codes, the program eliminates the duplicates and that's why one of the individuals is not recognized.

Someone know what can I do to conserve the two photos and the adult and cub can be recognized?

THANKS!

messages.author: 9c3183af58028473
messages.subject: Re: Individual identification
parts:
Alejandra
 
I solve this kind of problem this way.  I use the directory structure method to create the species and station columns in the recordTable R data frame.  I.e not the tag method.  So I just create another species folder.   Where I have two different species in the one image, I have an original and a copy of the same image in two species folders.

I am too slow to be able to explain how I would do this with tag and tag-method (metadata-method) to create the recordTable.

Regards
David

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Individual identification
parts:
Yes, David's method of creating a copy of the image in another directory should work.
Alternatively, using metadata tags, one would (in theory) only have to assign two tags for the two different individuals to the same image.

In both cases, recordTableIndividual should tease the records apart and return them as two separate individuals.

But please let us know what you did so we can help you.
